text:
Monzo UK savings interest rates range from 2.80% to 5.25% AER depending on the type of savings pot you choose and whether you pay for a Monzo subscription plan.   
DepositScout

(Note: Regular Monzo budgeting "Pots" and current account balances pay 0% interest — you must specifically open a Savings Pot or Cash ISA Pot.)

1. Instant Access Savings & Cash ISA (Variable)

Paid monthly on the 1st, with unlimited instant withdrawals and no minimum deposit (£1 for Cash ISA). Your rate depends on your Monzo subscription tier:   
Abel

Monzo Free: 2.80% AER   
The Finance Lowdown

Monzo Extra (£3/month): 3.15% AER   
The Finance Lowdown

Monzo Perks (£9/month): 3.55% AER   
The Finance Lowdown

Monzo Max (£19/month): 3.80% AER   
The Finance Lowdown

2. Select Access Savings & Cash ISA (Variable)

Requires a £500 minimum deposit and pays interest monthly. You get a higher rate as long as you make 2 or fewer withdrawals per year from that pot:

Monzo Free & Extra: 3.45% AER   
The Finance Lowdown

Monzo Perks & Max: 3.70% AER   
The Finance Lowdown

The catch: If you make a 3rd withdrawal before your pot's anniversary, the interest rate drops significantly (below the standard Instant Access rate) until the pot resets.   
Abel

3. Fixed Rate Savings & Cash ISA (Fixed)

Requires a £500 minimum deposit. Paid plans do not boost these rates — every tier gets the exact same rate, paid out at maturity:   
DepositScout
+ 1

1-Year Fixed: 4.70% AER   
DepositScout

2-Year Fixed: 5.10% AER   
DepositScout

3-Year Fixed: 5.25% AER   
DepositScout

4. 1p Saving Challenge Pot (Variable)

If you participate in Monzo's automated 1p-a-day challenge (which saves £667.95 over a year), that specific pot earns 5.00% AER on the balance.   
Monzo

Quick Tip on Paid Plans: Because paid plans charge a monthly fee, upgrading purely for a higher savings rate only makes financial sense if you hold a large balance. For example, upgrading from Free to Perks (£9/month = £108/year) gets you an extra 0.75% on Instant Access — you would need to hold at least £14,400 in savings just to break even on the subscription fee.
